steps.what: Read the actual water-level gauges and observe the weather conditions at the bridge or lock, resolving suspect readings.
Enter the actual water levels, weather observations and exceptions into the operating log in {OPS_SYSTEM}; a native entry form supplies only the station identifier, units and current entry time.
Check the logged water levels, observation time, units and weather conditions against the actual observations, correcting late entries and unusual readings in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Save the actual entry in the same operating log {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Configure the existing operating-log form to supply repeated station, units and entry-time fields. Keep actual gauge reading, weather observation, value entry and correction. OTHER means the site's gauges; no new sensor feed or observation-free capture is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each entry may repeat the same station and units in an otherwise manual log.
tasks.enabler_now: Native default fields and date-time controls can remove that repeated field entry where an electronic log already exists.
tasks.still_hard: A late entry needs its true observation time, and a plausible number can still be a faulty gauge reading.
tasks.human_edge: Relate changing water and weather to the actual site.

ambition.what: Maintain the same actual operating log.

tasks.altitude: Specify which fields are defaults and which must always be observed.

evidence.claim: Native form defaults can supply repeated station metadata without measuring water or weather.

assumptions: Conditional baseline is an existing electronic log with repeated manual station, units and entry-time fields; shares are estimates, not measured observations.
The 35% cut within entry removes those repeated fields only; all new observed values and exception text remain.
A pre-existing automatic logger earns no new saving here.
unknowns: Whether the actual log is paper or electronic and which fields are already supplied
research_questions: Time an actual entry and identify the repeated fields before enabling defaults.

already_counted.description: Actual observations, retained entry, value checks and ordinary save

incremental.description: Maintain station defaults and test time-zone/unit changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conservative case is a paper log or an electronic form already supplying all station metadata; the actual entry and observation work remain and no change is deployed. In the eligible manual-metadata case, s2 removes 15.75 hours per 100, less 1 hour of upkeep. Late timestamps and real readings remain manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect the actual operating-log entries, photographs, incident references and site procedure relevant to the accident in {DOCS}.
inputs: Actual existing operating records and incident material
outputs: Source package with times and references

steps.what: Clarify the actual accident sequence with the people involved and capture attributed statements and unresolved points in the report notes in {DOCS}.
outputs: Actual attributed notes and unresolved contradictions

steps.what: Draft the accident report chronology and narrative in {DOCS} from the actual source package and attributed notes, leaving missing facts and disputed causes explicit.

loop.purpose: Draft the accident narrative without resolving evidence disputes
loop.input: Actual selected incident records and attributed notes from s1-s2
loop.output: Source-linked chronology and narrative with explicit unknowns
loop.check: Tender checks every factual claim, attribution and report attachment in s5
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved chronology or missing facts return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Use the native report template first; free-text accounts still need a narrative, and literal field mapping cannot determine what an attributed sentence says.

steps.what: Populate the report's repeated incident identifier, station details and attachment-reference table in the native {DOCS} report template from the selected actual records.
inputs: Actual selected incident identifiers and attachment references from s1
outputs: Complete draft accident report with reference table

steps.what: Check the completed accident report against the evidence, correct chronology and attribution, and authorise that final version and its actual recipient for dispatch under the incident procedure.
inputs: Complete draft accident report from s4
Actual evidence and attributed notes from s1-s2
outputs: Final accident report and dispatch authorisation bound to its version and recipient

steps.what: Save the final accident report in the same {DOCS} incident folder.
Send the final accident report to its actual authorised recipient through {EMAIL}, only for the version and recipient authorised in s5.

tasks.design: Use the native incident template for exact fields and a bounded drafting pass for the actual evidence narrative. Preserve gathering, attributed conversations and full factual checking. The send remains separate; an ordinary internal save is ungated. Any report or recipient change invalidates the dispatch authorisation and returns to s5.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual evidence is spread across logs and accounts, and composing a chronology takes manual writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Template field mapping and source-linked draft generation can reduce the assembly without deciding fault.
tasks.still_hard: Contradictory accounts and absent observations cannot be filled in by the drafting system.
tasks.human_edge: Give accurate first-hand evidence and distinguish facts from inference.

ambition.what: Produce the existing required accident report.

tasks.altitude: Define the report's evidence and attribution standard.

evidence.claim: A report template can populate exact fields, while bounded text drafting still requires source and attribution review.

assumptions: Conditional existing workflow includes a report sent to an incident recipient; no extra reporting campaign is added.
Actual records are produced by normal operations; actual witness clarification and notes are counted in s2.
Shares are design estimates; narrative remainder includes correction and manual fallback, not only reading.
unknowns: Actual report template, access restrictions and required recipient
Whether narrative drafting is permitted for incident evidence
research_questions: Test a permitted completed case for unsupported facts, attribution errors and actual drafting effort.

already_counted.description: Actual evidence gathering, accounts, narrative repair, final check, save and dispatch

incremental.description: Maintain report field mappings and check source-link behaviour after changes

approvals.approved_version: Final report content and actual recipient checked in s5; any change requires s5 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A contested accident with incomplete records may require wholly manual narration and attachment assembly; no deployment or saving in that conservative case. With permitted comparable source material, narrative assembly removes 13.5 hours and repeated fields remove 10, while all 18 hours of final checking remain; subtract 2 hours upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the bridge deck, approaches and actual observation views for vehicles and pedestrians prior to opening; look directly where required by the site procedure.
inputs: Actual bridge, approaches and existing observation views

steps.what: Resolve obscured areas and uncertain vehicle or pedestrian positions, holding the opening sequence while obtaining a clear actual view or necessary live confirmation.
inputs: Current observations and unresolved areas from s1
outputs: Resolved actual clearance information or opening held

steps.what: Determine from the actual current bridge-clearance observations whether the bridge is clear of vehicles and pedestrians; otherwise retain the hold.
outputs: Current human clearance decision or hold

tasks.design: Retain the actual clearance check. OTHER is the existing bridge observation equipment and physical site. Native view selection, detector alerts and existing interlocks were considered: they do not remove the required actual viewing and resolution in this baseline. Do not invent a written clearance report, duplicate control-room transcription or an automatic opening.
tasks.previous_blocker: Seeing an empty image is not proof that every part of a bridge is clear.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing observation aids can support the tender, but no changed human action is established here.
tasks.still_hard: Occlusion, unexpected movement and loss of a view require immediate site-specific judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Hold operations when the actual bridge cannot be confirmed clear.

ambition.what: Perform the existing physical clearance check.

tasks.altitude: Know the actual observation limits and hold criteria.

evidence.claim: Observation aids do not establish a safe labour reduction without proving their coverage against the site's actual clearance procedure.

assumptions: No separate manual written record, copied report or sent message is established for this check; none is added to the baseline.
Existing control-system event capture is runtime, not manual labour removed by this proposal.
Bridge movement is a separate actual operation, not an uncounted proposed machine action.
unknowns: Site coverage and mandated visual-check sequence
research_questions: Observe the actual clearance cycle and identify whether any distinct manual duplicate entry really exists.

already_counted.description: All actual viewing, uncertainty resolution and clearance decision

incremental.description: No changed workflow or additional equipment proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: After separating actual viewing, uncertainty resolution and the decision, no existing written report, re-key or send is evidenced. Native alerts or view presets do not remove any required check. All existing work remains; zero is not inferred merely from safety sensitivity.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the actual barrier, signal and drawbridge status and give the live decision to raise the drawbridge under the site operating procedure; a prior deck-clearance check must still be current.
inputs: Actual barrier, signal and bridge states
outputs: Current raise decision for this actual bridge cycle or hold

steps.what: Issue the actual raise-drawbridge command on {OPS_SYSTEM} only under the current live raise decision from s1.
inputs: Current cycle-specific raise decision from s1

steps.what: Observe the drawbridge raising and the passage of actual water traffic, staying at the controls and stopping the sequence if the actual conditions require it.
inputs: Actual drawbridge movement and water traffic after s2
outputs: Actual monitored passage and any stop condition

steps.what: Check that the actual water traffic has cleared the moving structure and determine whether the drawbridge can now be lowered, holding for any uncertainty.
inputs: Actual completed or ongoing passage from s3
outputs: Current live lower decision for this cycle or hold

steps.what: Issue the actual lower-drawbridge command on {OPS_SYSTEM} only under the current lowering decision from s4.
inputs: Current cycle-specific lower decision from s4

steps.what: Observe actual lowering and confirm the bridge is in its required road position with the relevant actual indications before deciding to raise the automobile gates.
outputs: Current automobile-gate release decision or hold

steps.what: Issue the actual raise-automobile-gates command on {OPS_SYSTEM} only for the live gate-release decision from s6.
Observe the actual automobile gates opening and road traffic resuming, remaining responsible for the actual bridge cycle and any immediate abnormal condition.
inputs: Actual gate movement and road traffic after s7

tasks.design: Keep the live physical operating sequence and each real equipment command separate. The command gates are actual moment-of-operation readiness decisions, not approvals of an author's saved text. Any changed state, delay or new traffic invalidates the associated live decision. Existing native interlocks and command event logging remain existing runtime and earn no saving. No extra written cycle record is invented.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bridge operation depends on the actual traffic and structure state throughout the movement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing controls support the tender; no new independently justified reduction in attendance or commands is established.
tasks.still_hard: An unexpected vessel, person or equipment indication can invalidate the sequence immediately.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain continuous situational attention and stop rather than infer clearance.

ambition.what: Complete the existing bridge passage cycle.

tasks.altitude: Understand hold conditions and the limits of current interlocks.

evidence.claim: Existing interlocked bridge controls do not themselves justify removing actual operational observation or treating existing runtime as new labour saving.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative active-work allocation for the existing operating cycle; no removed unattended waiting is claimed.
The prior bridge-clearance check is an existing prerequisite, not a new free machine input or a claimed saving handed to another answer.
No separate manually written operating report is established within this action; automatic controller event capture already occurs without new tender labour.
unknowns: Actual control sequence, interlock behaviour and attendance requirements
research_questions: Observe one complete bridge cycle and distinguish actual attended work from controller runtime before considering any change.

already_counted.description: All actual decisions, individual commands and attended observation

incremental.description: No new operating workflow or automation proposed

approvals.approved_version: Live bridge cycle and actual states checked in s1; changed state requires s1 again
Actual passage and lowering conditions checked in s4; changed state requires s4 again
Actual lowered bridge and gate-release states checked in s6; changed state requires s6 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: After splitting each actual equipment command from its live decision and observation, the existing native interlocks remove no new tender action. No manual copied report or send is evidenced. Continuous observation and the small commands remain fully retained, rather than claiming existing controller runtime as a new reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Define reliable log fields and evidence standards while retaining live responsibility for bridge and lock conditions.
role.ambitious_version: A tender who spends less time repeating log metadata and assembling evidence, while keeping actual observation and control decisions.
